Further, looking at the space heating (red) lines in both residential and commercial sectors, we can see that about 85% customers in the residential and over 90% customers in the commercial sector have a payback period of 3 years or under when on the Full tariff. Whereas space cooling curves in dark blue shows that 97% residential and 93% commercial customers have a payback period of 3 years or less. This difference in response between heating and cooling is expected because the cooling load is still quite coincident with the system net load peaks in 2030 and provides an opportunity to save more than space heating. On the Mild tariff, we still see a substantial number of customers with very low payback periods, particularly in the residential sector where there is expected to be significant adoption of connected thermostats that do not need to be paid off by price response. However, particularly in the commercial sector, a much wider range of payback period results are observed. Only 20% of commercial cooling customers have a payback period less than 3 years, and about half of customers have a payback period above 5 years. Finally, the third panel of Figure 28 shows the payback period distribution for agricultural crop irrigation load. On the Full tariff, we see that 60% of customers with pumping load have a payback period of 3 years or less. These are large customers that can offset the high initial costs of the technology with similar savings. Smaller customers tend to experience the high fixed costs with moderate bill savings, thus extending the time required to recover the costs. Distribution of payback period by end use for the Full tariff design (top) and Mild tariff design (bottom) 3.4.4 Resulting economic potential This section explores the magnitude of three levels of flexibility potential that consider various thresholds for costs. The technical potential is the total magnitude of possible load flexibility, regardless of costs, cost-effective potential is the value of the resource in each end use that has a cost-benefit ratio of 1 or lower, regardless of payback period, and short payback potential is the value of the resource in each end use that has a payback period of 3 years or less. This represents the resources that may be enabled based on typical technology procurement decision making methods. Figure 29 shows the comparison of technical, cost effective, and short payback potential of four metrics across the three tariff design scenarios; these values are tabulated in Tables 5-8. Patterns of results across tariffs and end uses are generally consistent across each metric, as the same set of resources is providing the potential. Therefore, results will be described in general terms across the four metrics for flexibility potential. The Full tariff (first panel) offers the most potential followed by Medium and Mild.
